title: Microsoft Azure Database Administrator Associate DP-300

nodes.title: Security fundamentals: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Security is about layering defenses so no single failure compromises a system. Most exams test the same core ideas: least privilege, defense in depth, the CIA triad, and the shared-responsibility line between you and your cloud provider.

flashcards.back: Confidentiality (only the right people see the data), Integrity (data isn't tampered with), Availability (the system is reachable when needed). Every security control maps to at least one of these three pillars.
Grant each identity (user, role, service account) the minimum permissions needed to do its job — no more. The opposite is wildcard access, which makes a single credential leak catastrophic.
Stack multiple, independent controls so an attacker has to defeat all of them. Example: WAF in front of an app, network ACL on the subnet, IAM on the workload, encryption at rest in the database.

flashcards.front: Shared responsibility model — who does what?
flashcards.back: The cloud provider secures the cloud (physical hardware, hypervisor, region facilities). You secure what's IN the cloud (your data, IAM config, OS patching on EC2, application code). The exact line shifts by service: serverless is more on the provider, IaaS is more on you.

nodes.title: Part 2: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 2. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Users report intermittent slow response from a stored procedure on Azure SQL Database. You need to identify the most expensive queries over the last hour, compare runtime statistics across recent plans, and force a known-good plan if needed - using a built-in feature with no extra extension. Which capability should you use?
flashcards.back: Query Store is built into Azure SQL Database and is enabled by default. It captures query texts, runtime statistics, and all execution plans, lets you compare plans over time, and supports sp_query_store_force_plan to pin a chosen plan. Extended Events can collect data but provide no plan-comparison UI or plan-forcing. Database Mail is for notifications. SQL Server Profiler is a legacy tool that is not supported against Azure SQL Database.

flashcards.front: A SaaS workload has 200 small Azure SQL Databases with bursty, unpredictable activity - only a handful are busy at any moment. You want them to share a pool of compute and storage to lower cost while still being billed as a single resource. Which feature fits best?
flashcards.back: Elastic pools are designed exactly for this pattern: many databases with low average and unpredictable peak utilization share a fixed set of vCores or DTUs, so you pay for the pool rather than for each database. Dedicated SQL pools are part of Synapse Analytics and are not for OLTP databases. Managed Instance is per-instance, not a shared pool for many small databases. Linked servers add cross-database querying, not resource sharing.

flashcards.front: You must migrate an on-premises SQL Server database to Azure with minimal code changes. The application depends on SQL Server Agent jobs, cross-database queries, CLR assemblies, and Service Broker. Which Azure database target should you choose?
flashcards.back: Azure SQL Managed Instance is the PaaS option with the highest compatibility with on-premises SQL Server. It supports SQL Server Agent, cross-database queries within the instance, CLR, Service Broker, Database Mail, and most other instance-scoped features. Azure SQL Database (single database) is database-scoped and lacks SQL Agent and cross-database queries. Cosmos DB is a different NoSQL engine. Azure Database for MySQL is a different RDBMS entirely.

flashcards.front: Compliance requires you to retain weekly full backups of an Azure SQL Database for 7 years, well beyond the maximum 35-day point-in-time restore window. Which feature should you configure?
flashcards.back: Long-term retention lets you keep automatic weekly, monthly, and yearly full backups for up to 10 years on Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance, satisfying multi-year compliance requirements. PITR caps at 35 days and cannot be raised higher. BACPAC exports are application-consistent but require manual scheduling and storage management, and a BACPAC is not a transactionally consistent full backup. Geo-redundant storage controls backup placement, not how long backups are kept.

nodes.title: Network operations (CompTIA Network+): Key Ideas
nodes.content: Network+ tests operational fundamentals: how SNMP works for device monitoring, why baseline documentation matters, the change-management process that prevents accidental outages, and syslog severity levels that tell you how serious a message is. These appear in scenario questions where you're asked which tool to use or which process was skipped.

flashcards.front: SNMP — OID, MIB, community string, v2c vs v3.
flashcards.back: OID (Object Identifier): a dotted-number path in the MIB tree that uniquely identifies one piece of device data (e.g., `1.3.6.1.2.1.2.2.1.10` = ifInOctets). MIB (Management Information Base): the schema/dictionary that maps OIDs to human-readable names. Community string: a plain-text password used for SNMP v1/v2c authentication — typically 'public' (read) and 'private' (write); a well-known security weakness. SNMPv3 replaces community strings with proper user-based auth (MD5/SHA) and encryption (AES/DES).

flashcards.front: Why is network baseline documentation critical?
flashcards.back: A baseline records normal traffic volumes, CPU/memory levels, error rates, and routing tables — captured during a known-good period. When something goes wrong, you compare current readings to the baseline to spot the anomaly (utilization spiked 300%, a new route appeared, error rate tripled). Without a baseline, 'high CPU' is meaningless because you don't know what 'normal' was. Network+ expects you to identify baselining as a best practice before troubleshooting.

flashcards.front: Change management process — what are the key steps?
flashcards.back: Request change → assess risk and impact → obtain approval (CAB or manager) → schedule a maintenance window → implement → test and verify → document outcome → close. The exam distinguishes emergency changes (faster approval path for critical incidents) from standard changes (pre-approved, low-risk, routine). Skipping change management is the most common cause of self-inflicted outages.

0 Emergency, 1 Alert, 2 Critical, 3 Error, 4 Warning, 5 Notice, 6 Informational, 7 Debug. Lower number = more severe. Most organizations alert on 0–3 and log 0–6. Debug (7) produces enormous volume and is usually enabled only during active troubleshooting. The mnemonic: Every Awful Crisis Erodes Wisdom, No Debate.

questions.q: You want Azure SQL Database to automatically detect query regressions caused by new execution plans, force the previous good plan, and create or drop indexes based on workload observations - with no scripting on your part. Which capability should you enable?
questions.explanation: Automatic tuning on Azure SQL Database can FORCE_LAST_GOOD_PLAN when a regression is detected, and (when enabled) CREATE_INDEX and DROP_INDEX based on Database Engine recommendations from workload analysis. Resource Governor caps resource consumption for workload groups; it does not change plans or indexes. Database Mail only sends emails. Change Data Capture tracks DML changes for downstream consumers, not query plans.

questions.q: An auditor requires that every successful and failed login, plus every change to server-level permissions, on an Azure SQL Database server be captured into long-term, query-friendly storage so the team can run KQL queries across years of records. Which audit destination should you choose?
choices: Azure Blob Storage with append blobs only
The Windows Security event log on the SQL host
A SQL table inside the same audited database
questions.explanation: Azure SQL auditing can write to a Log Analytics workspace, where audit events are queryable with Kusto Query Language (KQL), can be retained for years, and can drive alerts and workbooks. Blob storage is supported but stores opaque .xel files and is not KQL-queryable on its own. There is no Windows Security event log surfaced for the PaaS service. Writing audit data to the audited database itself is not a supported destination and would create a chain-of-custody problem.

questions.q: A reporting application repeatedly runs long SELECT queries against an Azure SQL Database on the Business Critical tier. You want these queries to run on a replica so they do not contend with the OLTP workload, without provisioning any additional database. What should you configure?
choices: Enable Change Data Capture and point reports at the CDC tables
Create a separate copy with database copy and refresh it nightly
Add a secondary in an active geo-replication relationship in the same region
Set the ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly connection string to use a built-in read scale-out replica
questions.explanation: Business Critical and Premium tiers include built-in read scale-out: AlwaysOn replicas are already part of the SLA, and connections with ApplicationIntent=ReadOnly are routed to one of those replicas at no extra cost and with no additional database to manage. CDC exposes change tables but does not offload general SELECT workload. A nightly copy is stale by hours. Active geo-replication adds a billed secondary database and is overkill when an in-tier read replica already exists.

questions.q: A production Azure SQL Database currently uses the default Azure-chosen maintenance window, and business owners are reporting unexpected short reconfiguration events during peak trading hours (08:00-17:00 local). You need future planned maintenance to happen outside business hours without changing the service tier. What should you do?
choices: Apply a non-default maintenance window such as Weekday 22:00-06:00
Scale up to a higher vCore size and resubmit the request
Open a support ticket each week to delay maintenance
Move the database to the Basic tier
questions.explanation: Azure SQL Database and Managed Instance support configurable maintenance windows. Selecting a non-default window (for example a weekday or weekend evening slot) tells the platform to perform planned maintenance only during that period, avoiding business hours. Scaling vCores changes performance but not when maintenance happens. Repeated support tickets are not a supported way to defer planned maintenance. Moving to Basic would degrade the service and still subject it to maintenance.
